title: Prove one-disk cutover readiness
goal: After the facts/hardware gate, managed-build implementation, disposable activation proof and storage-rehearsal harness are terminal and reviewed, prove one-disk NixOS cutover readiness on an exclusively reserved disposable non-production target: rehearse the exact canonical LUKS2+Btrfs topology from a blank virtual disk, restore independently sourced off-host backup material, reconstruct and boot a fresh system, prove offline recovery, and finish with a reviewed evidence-complete cutover plan whose actual production device remains deliberately unbound for a later separately authorized destructive order.

approval.note: Runtime/block-device mutation is authorized only inside the exclusively reserved disposable service.heim-pc-nixos-storage-rehearsal-sandbox and only with the exact terminal reviewed T005 harness. The productive Heim-PC block devices, EFI, Secure-Boot, firmware, boot state and OS remain outside this authority.

acceptance.assertion: Before any block-device/runtime effect, the run is bound to the exact terminal T005 source revision and independent review evidence; the rehearsal implementation is read-only for T003 and any dirty state, revision drift or missing review fails closed.

Before sgdisk, wipefs, cryptsetup luksFormat, mkfs or boot mutation, the run holds the exclusive service.heim-pc-nixos-storage-rehearsal-sandbox claim and fresh independent evidence proves the target is a blank disposable virtual disk whose backing is not the productive Heim-PC root/system disk, not any mounted production filesystem and not production EFI/firmware state; ambiguity fails closed before effect.

Starting from the independently proven blank disposable virtual disk, the exact production-target topology GPT + EFI System Partition + recovery/boot-recovery surface + LUKS2 + Btrfs with @root, @nix, @persist, @home, @data and @containers is created, LUKS unlock is proven, every Btrfs subvolume is mounted correctly, the resulting disposable system actually boots, and independent readback proves the expected topology; the earlier LUKS+ext4 VM proof is not substituted for this gate.

Fresh read-only inventory classifies every migration-relevant non-reproducible data class separately from caches and rebuildable state; current scoped backup success is not treated as proof of complete cutover coverage.

Every critical migration data class is covered by sufficient physically/logically independent off-host storage and a staged realistic restore into the disposable rehearsal sandbox proves representative usable content; a capacity-constrained, production-disk-backed or non-independently-restorable backup target cannot satisfy this gate.

A fresh disposable system is reconstructed from the reviewed declarative state plus independently restored non-reproducible data, demonstrating that neither hidden production-host state nor the original system disk is required for recovery.

Independent bootable recovery media plus the required offline host/control closure, source/lock/trust roots and LUKS/recovery material are verified without Grabowski, Bureau, network or the production system SSD.

The cutover plan defines the exact later device-binding procedure and required fresh evidence for model, serial number, mounts, root backing, health and recovery readiness, but deliberately leaves the actual production block-device identity unbound until a separate destructive cutover order authorizes it; historical WD_BLACK SN850X/nvme0n1 evidence is orientation only.

The terminal artifact is a reviewed evidence object/plan binding the approved activation-proof evidence, exact target topology, point of no return, rollback/reconstruction procedure, mandatory post-boot readback and all prerequisite backup/recovery evidence, while containing no current authorization or production block-device binding for the real cutover.

Although destructive commands are required inside the exclusive disposable sandbox, this task terminates before sgdisk, wipefs, cryptsetup luksFormat, mkfs, real EFI-partition mutation, Secure-Boot key mutation, firmware write, productive nixos-install, productive switch or reboot into a new production OS on the Heim-PC; such effects require a later explicit destructive-action order bound to fresh production-device and recovery evidence.

Exact target-preflight, VM/storage topology, boot/readback, backup restore, fresh reconstruction, offline recovery and final-plan evidence are independently reviewed before T003 is considered terminal.

metadata.historical_device_reference_not_authorit: WD_BLACK SN850X 2TB / historical nvme0n1 orientation only; actual production device identity is intentionally unbound in this task
